findings.body: internal/reconcile/dispatch.go claimDispatch calls classificationFor on every implement-tick claim, after counting failed prior attempts, and classificationFor asks whenever no record exists and a classifier is set. The comment there says 'at the FIRST DISPATCH ... and nowhere else' and the classify.go header says 'never configured' is recorded, but a nil classifier records nothing. So a run whose attempt 1 ran with no classifier and failed, resumed with one, asks at attempt 2 and dispatches at dear_tier plus one rung (e.g. strong) where the warm process dispatches at default plus one (balanced). That is a cold/warm divergence driven by state outside git, plus a rung the failure never earned. Fix: ask only when the tick has no prior attempt (otherwise read-or-fallback), or record a 'no classifier configured' no-answer at first dispatch; add a restart test where the classifier's presence changes between incarnations.
findings.title: Classify only at a role-less tick's first dispatch: a later attempt with no record must not ask

findings.body: widthForWave (internal/reconcile/window.go) and recordTierPolicy (profiles.go) derive a wave's tiers with TierPolicy.Derive, which uses a nil classification, while dispatch uses DeriveClassified with the recorded one. With host width 3, concurrency.balanced = 1, and three role-less ticks whose recorded mass clears the threshold, width stays 3 and three dear-tier dispatches run concurrently, and the planning line says the wave is not narrowed. Read the recorded classification (read-only, never ask) when computing first-attempt tiers for width.
findings.title: tier_policy.concurrency ignores classification-promoted starts when sizing a wave

findings.body: Epic wne added RoleClassifyTick to runstate.DecisionRoles() in Go, but cloudflare/src/run-state-store.ts validateDecision still checks role against ROLES only. decision() throws 'unreadable decision', decisions() goes through decision() and throws too, and epic-reconciler.ts calls decisions() at lines 627 and 1041. A run branch carrying a classification therefore breaks every decisions() read on the Workflow host. It is latent until a classifier is wired, and it is a Go/TS parity break in stores documented as mirrors.
findings.title: TS run-state store throws on a classify-tick decision record the Go reconciler writes

findings.body: The gate runs go test -short, and 7 of the 10 tests exercising epic wne's exchange and routing (the four end-to-end classify_test.go exchange tests and the three tier_test.go mass-routing tests) skip under -short; only three pure record-parsing tests ran at each tick's gate. They pass in a full run (verified in review), but per-tick gates went green without exercising the change. Either give the gate a non-short run of the packages a tick touched, or make these fixture tests cheap enough not to skip.
findings.title: The in-run go gate skips every end-to-end classification and mass-routing test (-short)

findings.body: Under a review-epic launch's GIT_CONFIG_* env (url.ticfac-read-only-grade://...pushInsteadOf='/' and friends), internal/reconcile's TestAStopThatNeedsAPersonStillStopsUnderSupervision, TestAResumableRefusalIsContinuedByTheRunAndCountedAsAnIntervention and TestTheSameRefusalOverAnUnchangedTreeHaltsInsteadOfSpinning fail with 'remote-ticfac-read-only-grade is not a git command', because the fixtures' pushes to local temp origins are rewritten too. They pass with the env stripped. A read-only reviewer therefore cannot run the suite the gate runs; fixtures should scrub the inherited GIT_CONFIG_* push keys the way they pin maintenance.auto.
findings.title: Review launches' pushInsteadOf rewrite breaks three supervise_test fixtures that push to temp repos
